title: Colorado Road Trip Itinerary
body:
Below is a photo-centric, light-hiking road-trip that fits the schedule you gave. I've added golden-hour windows, drive times, and food stops that match your Thai/South-Asian/Mexican tastes (plus a few irresistibly charming spots). Distances assume fair weather; add buffer if afternoon storms build in the high country.

---

Tuesday - 20 May - Denver -> Estes Park

Time Plan Notes
2:30 pm Land at DEN, pick up rental Have water & snacks handy--altitude starts climbing fast.
3:15 pm I-25 N -> US-36 to Estes Park (~1 h 45 m) Big-Thompson Canyon turn-outs offer first glacier-carved-valley shots.
5:00 pm Check-in Lakeside or downtown lodges keep you close to sunset views.
6:00 pm (Golden hour: 7:40-8:20 pm) Walk the Estes Riverwalk -> Lake Estes Marina Panoramic reflections of the Mummy Range.
7:15 pm Dinner at Cafe de Pho Thai (fresh Thai curries) or Nepal's Cafe (Nepali/Indian comfort) Both are casual, kid-friendly.
After dark Short drive up to the Stanley Hotel overlook for night-sky shots (minimal light pollution).

---

Wednesday - 21 May - RMNP Dawn -> Royal Gorge -> Colo. Springs

Time Plan Notes
4:45 am (Sunrise ~ 5:39 am) Enter Rocky Mountain NP (no timed-entry needed until 24 May) Sprague Lake (0.5 mi loop) is flat, photogenic, and moose-friendly.
7:45 am Bear Lake loop or out-and-back to Alberta Falls (2 mi RT) Easy grade, waterfall framed by snow-flecked peaks.
9:30 am Return, quick hotel breakfast, check out
10:30 am Scenic drive US-34 -> I-25 S -> Canon City (~3 h 20 m) Coffee stop in Monument for views of the Front Range.
2:00 pm Royal Gorge Bridge & Park walk-about Shoot the 955-ft-deep canyon from both bridge towers.
4:00 pm Late lunch at El Caporal (classic Mexican) in Canon City
5:00 pm Drive to Colorado Springs (~1 h) & check-in
6:30 pm (Golden hour: 7:50-8:10 pm) Garden of the Gods - High-Point & Balanced Rock Flaming sandstone spires back-lit at sunset.
8:30 pm Dinner: NaRai Thai or trendy tacos at Dos Santos

---

Thursday - 22 May - Colorado Springs (flex)
- Sunrise 5:41 am -- join the quiet Siamese Twins sunrise walk in Garden of the Gods (5:30 am start, flat 1-mi loop).
- Late morning: drive the short, photo-rich Garden of the Gods loop or head 40 min east to the pastel hoodoos of Paint Mines Interpretive Park (1.5-mi easy loop).
- Lunch: Thai Mint (authentic Issan dishes) or Uchenna for a fascinating Ethiopian detour.
- Afternoon options (pick one):
- Pikes Peak Summit (14,115 ft) via the new cog-railway (reserve) or personal vehicle (very light walking on top).
- Broadmoor Seven Falls paved walk & stair climb (choose lower viewpoints if you prefer fewer steps).
- Dinner & blue hour: Stroll historic Old Colorado City--sunset paints the adobe storefronts; grab dessert crepes at La Baguette.

---

Friday - 23 May - Colo. Springs -> Georgetown -> Vail

Time Plan Notes
8:00 am Depart; I-25 N -> US-285/CO-470 -> I-70 W (~2 h) Aim to reach Georgetown by 11:30 am.
11:45 am Pick up tickets for Georgetown Loop RR (12:30 pm ride) Open-air cars = great canyon shots; ride is 1 h 15 m.
1:45 pm Grab a sandwich at The Happy Cooker or Thai noodles at Mountain Thai in Idaho Springs (10 min west).
2:30 pm Continue on I-70 to Vail (~1 h 15 m), optional stop at Dillon Reservoir overlook for alpine-lake vistas.
4:00 pm Check-in Vail; wander Gore Creek Trail & covered bridges.
7:45 pm sunset Gore Range alpenglow from Lionshead Village pedestrian deck.
Dinner Annapurna Nepali/Indian for curries & momos, or El Segundo (street-style Mexican) along the creek.

---

Saturday - 24 May - Vail & Summit County

Morning:
- If gondolas are running (check week-of), ride Eagle Bahn to Eagle's Nest & walk the 1-mi Fireweed Trail (mostly level, 10,500 ft views).
- Otherwise drive 20 min to Frisco and take the gentle 1-mi Rainbow Lake trail--wildflowers, peak reflections.

Mid-day: Brunch at The Little Diner (German-style pancakes) or poke bowls at Yellowbelly.

Afternoon choices:
1. Betty Ford Alpine Gardens (world's highest botanical garden, flat paths).
2. Scenic drive to Minturn for the quaint railroad-era Main St.; browse artists' stalls (Sat. market opens at 9 am).
3. Spa time at Vail Vitality Center--altitude massages and a killer mountain-view deck.

Dinner & Blue Hour: Creek-side patio at Sweet Basil (fine-dining charm) or casual enchiladas at La Cantina. Night-sky shots along Gore Creek footbridge.

---

Sunday - 25 May - Vail -> Denver Int'l (flight 17:00)

Time Plan Notes
7:00 am Sunrise stroll (5:40 am) along Gore Creek -> Betty Ford Gardens--flowers illuminated from the east.
9:00 am Quick bites/coffee at Yeti's Grind; pack up.
12:30 pm Depart Vail (2 h drive + typical Sunday I-70 traffic). Stop in Idaho Springs for a final Thai fix or a snap of Mount Evans from the overlook.
3:00 pm Rental-car return at DEN; TSA lines can be long on holiday weekends--aim to be curbside 2 h before.
5:00 pm Wheels-up, camera full!

---

Handy Tips
- Altitude: Estes (7,522 ft) -> Vail (8,150 ft). Pace hydration and avoid heavy booze the first 24 h.
- Weather layers: Mountain temps swing 40 F daily; pack puffy + rain shell.
- RMNP timed-entry starts 24 May; you're inside the free-flow window on the 21st, but reserve if you decide to return later.
- Wildlife photography: Stay 75 ft from elk/mule deer, 120 ft from moose.
- Leave No Trace: Stick to durable surfaces on all light-hike trails.

Have an unforgettable photo-filled week in the Rockies--may your memory cards and bellies be equally full!
